messages.subject: Follow-up | External affairs and social-value execution across BHP growth
messages.body:
Dear Ms. Cox,

I wanted to follow up on my note of 30 September with a more specific proposition around BHP's External Affairs agenda. BHP is moving into its next leadership phase with growth concentrated in copper and potash while continuing to define social value as a source of trusted partnership and long-term performance. That combination makes execution at the government, community and operating interface strategically important.

The capability I would bring is a disciplined model for turning external commitments into operating accountability. Around major projects and country operations, government relationships, community expectations, social investment, permitting, reputation risk and internal decision-making often move on different timelines. My experience has been built around bringing those streams together and giving senior management clear ownership, evidence and escalation.

As Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, I lead or coordinate government and regulatory engagement, ESG and social performance, corporate affairs, executive communications and stakeholder strategy. I work across operations, environment, HSE, legal, HR, finance, procurement, security and technical teams and support stakeholder governance around industrial renewable-energy and carbon-accounting programs.

If there is value in adding this kind of operating-side external-affairs leadership to BHP's regional, country or growth-project teams, I would welcome a confidential conversation. I have refined the attached CV around BHP's social-value, government-relations and growth-execution priorities rather than a generic sustainability profile.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department | AGM Inc.
